summary: Andrew Goudie is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall (BA, MA, PhD). He served as Head and Professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Indologist Andrew Henry Yarrow earned a B.A. at UNC Chapel Hill and a Ph.D. at Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He taught Sanskrit at Yale (~1950–1951), Indian languages and civilization at Columbia (1952), and became a professor at the University of Miami.

Andrew Hollingworth Frost was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at St John's College (B.A. 1838–1842). He served as Principal of Church Missionary Society College, Islington (1870–1874) and Lecturer in Marathi and Gujarati at Cambridge (1884–1902).

Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under Sri Narayana Mishra. As attested in 2026, he is an Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University.
Andrew Jukes was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Blundell's School. He served as a medical missionary for the Church Mission Society from 1878 to 1906.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (2014).

Andrew Ollett, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at the University of Oxford (~2008–2010) and Columbia University (~2010–2017). Around 2020, he was appointed Associate Professor at the University of Chicago.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Harvard and completed his doctorate at Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill (~1963–1967). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1967 to 2001.

Andrew Stirling was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at East India Company College (1811–1812) and Fort William College (~1813–1814). He served in the East India Company's Political Department from around 1828 to 1830.

Andrew Watsky is a Japanology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1987–1994). He held a post at Vassar College from around 1994 to 2008.

Andrew William Kennedy, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisors Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Indologist and linguist Andrey Klebanov earned his MA and Dr. Phil. at the University of Hamburg, supervised by Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Kyoto University professor (2016–2021), University of Alberta fellow (2021), and University of Vienna assistant (2022–2026).

Andrey Terentyev is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and earned his Ph.D. at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1980–1983). He held a post at the Museum of History of Religion (~1978–1992).
Andrey Zaliznyak studied under Vyacheslav Ivanov from around 1953 to 1958 and under André Martinet from around 1956 to 1957.

Indologist and linguist Andrzej Gawroński studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig (PhD 1908). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917), University of Lviv as Professor of Indology (1917), and the University of Warsaw (1920).

Andrzej Ługowski was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University and the University of Warsaw, completing a doctorate under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (~1961–1968). He subsequently taught at the University of Warsaw.

András Róna-Tas is a Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. He was a professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002) and president of the IATS (~1979–1985).

André Bareau was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at ENS, EPHE, and the Sorbonne under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at CNRS (1942–1955), EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France as professor (1971–1991).
